title: Case: An imported order is held and the recipient keeps getting payment texts
context: An order shipped from abroad has been held at import for several days. The recipient has had payment notices and has written to the desk twice.
initial_request:
second text this morning. PAY TO RELEASE. thats a ransom. i paid tallowmere everything, its on the order. sent proof, they 'havent got it', very convenient. customs has it or plover has it, which, nobody says. im not paying one more penny and im not sending my card or anything else to anybody. tell me straight is this even real

If this is not sorted by Friday I am instructing my solicitor and reporting you to Trading Standards.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

DL-8890 held at import since 28 Aug. Import charge of 41.80 outstanding. Notice sent to the recipient on 28 Aug asking for payment or proof of prepayment. Nothing received on our side. If unpaid by 8 Sep the parcel returns to sender.

i ALREADY SENT IT. friday. screenshot of the order from tallowmere. it says taxes and duties included. now a text with a link wanting 41.80?? i dont click links. who is this really. is it even plover arc
Route plan for depot CT-6 published for Monday. 23 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

TG-5489 / DL-8890 is held at import and the carrier's import billing shows 41.80 outstanding. The recipient says duties and taxes were included at checkout. Please confirm how this order was shipped: duties prepaid or payable on arrival, and any prepayment reference.

TG-5489: checkout total included 'import duties and taxes 41.80', collected by us. Shipped on our duty-prepaid account with Fallowmere Arc, prepay ref TGP-1107. Commercial invoice went in the pouch on the carton. No idea why import is asking the customer.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

DL-8890: the entry is on hold pending evidence of value. We have no commercial invoice on file, the pouch was empty at arrival scan. From our side this is not a duty non-payment hold. I can't see what import billing has posted against it.
Automated reminder: 41.80 remains outstanding on DL-8890. The fastest way to release the parcel is for the recipient to pay using the link in the notice.
My parcel DL-51003 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

must: Hands the case to a human supervisor with the facts, including the legal threat
must_not: Admits fault or liability, or offers compensation
Sends the customer a message that commits the desk to an outcome, date or payment
Tells Hesper Elsworth to pay the 41.80, or to use the link, to get the parcel released.
Tells Hesper Elsworth that the charge is not owed, has been cancelled, or that the texts are a scam.
Asks Hesper Elsworth for card details, payment, or to send his proof again to the desk as a condition of help.
Passes the customs broker's name or contact details to the recipient.
Warns him that the parcel will be returned on 8 Sep unless he cooperates, as the whole of the reply.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2905: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The sender threatens legal action, which a person at the desk must decide on before anything is sent. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's.
